text: Let's say efficient, faster scanning procedure. That is called active scanning. So, what is the active scanning? The active scanning is very similar, okay. The result is the same. But is faster. Why is faster? Because if your Wi-Fi card is configured to apply active scanning, when it tunes itself on a frequency channel, it does not just passively wait there for possible beacons, but is actually solicited the transmission of beacons. That means you will send a packet, a broadcast packet, saying, I'm a Wi-Fi card here. I would like to know who is operating on this frequency channel. Okay, so it solicited the access points that may be there to send a beacon. It does not just wait passively. Okay, so that's the difference, and this speeds up the process. Because if you ask, who is there? Then the access points that are there will reply to you, and you acquire all the information of the available access points more quickly. And then you move to the second channel again. You ask, who is there? You receive the answer, and then.
